about: sdn_classify's blind held-out set (C1939), built 2026-11-02 by a fresh context that never saw the classifier's prompt or the schema's guidance, from the locked answer key (tests/fixtures/blind_sets/sdn_classify/blind_answer_key.md, sha256 11a6ccee4457525106f3fd72fd209021c618faf5f06f9519f496bd0d1c5a851a; its draw blind_draw.json) and Mercury's evidence packs as kept when each detection fired in the blind runs of 2026-10-29 (sessions 1 to 3, the operator's run notes). One case per response the loop raised (the detection it would classify); a switch's sighting that joined another response as seen also is not a case. Each section is the pack's sdn section exactly as kept. Each detection is the loop's, rebuilt from its pack: the pack's detection piece, its key the alert's fingerprint (checked equal to detect.detection_key of its rule, network, connection, switch and subject), its subject from the alert's labels, and for a flood its sources the source addresses of the flows it rests on (the flood rule's own _flow_sources); the responses record was not read (it is in the network's data folder under data/lists/, which this builder was told not to read), so a field the loop kept beside these (its incident stamp) is absent; none of those is read by the classifier or its check. The packs predate C2237's reply marking: a flood's victim and a transfer's receivers are named sources here, as the loop named them then. Expectations are the key's rows, never edited, translated to the judge's fields: a scan's action rate_limit_source (the key's scan line), a flood's rate_limit_source or drop_source (the key's flood line, drop where allowed: the SDN lab's flood policy allows it), an unauthorised flow's remove_flow, a benign row's threat_detected false, threat_type none, severity none and action none; the severity the row's own; cites_any the ids the detection rests on as sent (an unauthorised flow's, the flow itself); where a response's own expectation is not written in the key (a link port naming no source, a victim or receiver named as the source, the scan rule's fallback firing on a flood), the case's edit says what the key's words imply and why. Counts: S1 1, S4 1, S3 1, BS1 1, BS3 1, F3 6, F5 1, F6 8, BF2 2, BF3 5, BF1 2, U1 1, U3 1, U6 1, BU1 1, BU2 1, BU3 2, BS4 1 (37 cases from 18 scenarios).
